title: Modulating cysteine metabolism to induce cell death in small cell lung cancer
text:
Small cell lung cancer is a deadly disease with few treatment options. This research will investigate how
manipulation of metabolism can trigger cell death in small cell lung cancer, potentially suggesting new treatment
strategies for this disease.

title: Identifying barriers and facilitators of harm reduction among adult dual users of e-cigarettes and cigarettes
text:
Dual use of e-cigarettes and cigarettes is common among adults in the United States. Most dual users report
using e-cigarettes with the intention of quitting; however, these cigarette smokers are faced with contextual
barriers/facilitators to harm reduction as well as daily triggers and settings associated with cigarette smoking.
This study proposes identifying these barriers/facilitators and daily triggers and settings of cigarette smoking in
adult dual users, which will provide evidence to help research and clinical practice for effective intervention
methods to address barriers to harm reduction.

title: Elucidating the Molecular Mechanisms that Mediate DKD Progression in Patients Living with HIV
text:
HIV-infected patients in the United States now live longer, owing to the effective antiretroviral therapy, but the
prevalence of chronic kidney disease continues to increase in this HIV-infected population due to comorbidities
with diabetes, hypertension, and HCV. This study will unravel the molecular mechanisms of how chronic HIV
infection contributes to the progression of age-related kidney disease, specifically diabetic kidney disease. The
knowledge gained will enable the development of effective targeted and personalized therapies.

title: A Scalable, Open-Source Generative LLM Tool for Automated Classification of Diagnostic Errors
text:
Medical errors contribute to significant patient harm, yet their full scope remains unclear. This
project leverages the Retract-and-Reorder (RAR) method and generative large language models
(LLMs) to automate the classification of order errors, validating the approach on diagnostic
imaging and medication orders with potential applications in other domains. By developing a
scalable, open-source pipeline, this work aims to enhance error detection, improve patient safety,
and enable cross-institutional implementation of AI-driven error classification tools.

title: Profiling and forecasting individual unique progression in ADRD using machine learning
text:
Early and accurate detection of ADRD is critical for timely intervention but is prohibitively difficult due to the large
heterogeneity among patients. No single diagnostic or prognostic tool is sufficient to fully explain the
heterogeneity of ADRD. To address this gap, the research and training for this Mentored Quantitative Research
Development Award will be centered on deploying a multi-modal information framework that integrates in vivo
and digital biomarkers sourced from existing longitudinal studies to improve diagnostic and prognostic
capabilities of ADRD.

title: Cognitively-enhanced tDCS of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex to reduce craving in cocaine addiction
text:
We will test whether cognitively enhanced transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) of the dorsolateral
prefrontal cortex can reduce craving in inpatients with cocaine use disorder. Neuroimaging before and after
stimulation will establish the neural correlates of recovery and allow predictions of outcomes, which will be
assessed throughout the study and one month after its completion. Results could pave the way towards
development of a new self-administered intervention to reduce craving when it is needed the most, enhancing
recovery real-time and in the natural environment in people with cocaine addiction as generalizable to other
drugs of abuse and other disorders of self-control.

title: Modeling and Analysis of the Spatio-Temporal Dynamics of the Mitochondrial Network
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because defects in mitochondria are at the heart of many
diseases including heart disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer. Therefore, the proposed research plan to
elucidate the fundamental principles underlying mitochondrial network morphology and dynamics is relevant to
the part of NIH's mission that seeks to mitigate the burden of human disease by developing fundamental
knowledge of the processes driving disease. In addition, the proposed work seeks to develop methodologies
that make mitochondria research more accessible to other researchers, thereby accelerating the advent of new
therapies.

title: Markey STRONG Scholars Program
text: Kentucky has the highest cancer incidence and mortality rates in the nation that derive from the state’s prevalent health, socioeconomic, and educational challenges. To help reverse these trends, The Markey Science Training in Research, Oncology, Networking and professional Growth (STRONG) Scholars Program will provide transformative mentored cancer research experiences for individuals from the communities most severely impacted by cancer with the goal of creating a more resilient, knowledgeable and innovative workforce in cancer research that is ready to effect change.

title: Determining mechanisms of heterogeneous treatment response in glioblastoma using multi-omic and multi-organ approaches
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor that nearly always recurs after treatment and has a very poor
prognosis. Despite its clinical importance, recurrent GBM remains poorly characterized at the molecular level.
This project will apply cutting-edge genomic tools—including spatial transcriptomics and long-read single-cell
RNA sequencing—to uncover mechanisms of recurrence and identify new therapeutic targets.

title: Chemical Approaches to Control the Function of Regulatory RNAs
text:
Double stranded RNAs are exciting regulatory molecules, powerful tools for basic biological sciences,
and targets for novel therapeutic approaches. This proposal will explore chemical modifications to optimize
the properties of such RNA molecules and study the mechanism of their action. If successful, the project will
create improved research tools, provide unique insights into structure and function of RNA and may open
doors for development of new drugs for diseases where the traditional pharmaceutics have been less
successful.

title: ESCAPE - Evaluation of Prostate Specific Membrane Antigen Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography in Active Surveillance for Prostate Cancer
text:
Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men and the second leading cause of cancer
death. Men with clinically insignificant prostate cancer are placed on active surveillance which
consists or repeat laboratory analysis, imaging, and prostate biopsy until patients progress to
clinically significant prostate at which point they need treatment. The objective of this proposal
is to explore the use of Prostate Specific Membrane Antigen Positron Emission Tomography-
Computed Tomography (PSMA-PET CT) in detecting clinically significant prostate cancer in
patients on active surveillance.

title: Core A: Biospecimen & Pathology Core
text: The Biospecimen and Pathology Core (BPC) will establish a biospecimen repository of anal cancer (AC) and cervical cancer (CC) from different population groups that have unique incidence and mortality rates. Through well-established, multi-institutional collaborations between the University of Miami/Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, Emory University/Winship Cancer Institute, and Morehouse School of Medicine, the BPC of the PeRsonalized Outreach and Multifaceted Interventions for Screening Enhancement (PROMISE) for Anal and Cervical Cancer Prevention and Treatment SPORE will acquire different types of biospecimens to support all PROMISE Projects and anticipated needs of innovative pilot studies proposed as part of the Career Enhancement Program (CEP), the Developmental Research Program (DRP), and outside collaborations. The BPC will enable translational researchers to conduct high impact investigations that will change cancer treatment and outcomes. The key functions of the BPC will be to provide PROMISE investigators with a standardized system for specimen collection, centralized pathology review, processing, storage, tracking, and distribution and will enable access to state-of-the-art laboratory technologies providing expertise in tissue-based assays and biomarker analyses. Comprehensive medical chart abstractions and data harmonization will ensure all biospecimens will be highly annotated with demographic, clinical, and social determinants of health data. Standardized quality control efforts and collaboration with the Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Core (BBC) will ensure rigor and reproducibility of all analyses. Prioritization of biospecimen usage will be determined by a Biospecimen Utilization Committee that will prioritize access to biospecimens and associated data based on the merit of the proposed translational cancer research. It is expected that the BPC will a) provide rapid and comprehensive expert morphologic assessment of experimental human tissue samples included in the proposed studies; b) produce high-quality, quantitative scoring data amenable to appropriate statistical tests of significance in collaboration with the BBC; c) ensure that all histopathologic analyses are conducted rigorously with appropriate quality assurance measures; d) provide all services in an efficient and cost-effective manner that is not redundant with other in-house resources; and e) ensure that patient biospecimens used for PROMISE SPORE studies are procured directly from the unique patient populations that are routinely cared for in the South Florida and Atlanta catchment areas of these institutions.

title: Low-Cost, User-Friendly SERS Technology for Rapid Detection of Emerging Drug Threats
text:
The misuse of synthetic opioids, pharmaceutical and veterinary drugs has intensified into a public health crisis,
fueling overdose deaths and substance use disorders. This project aims to develop a cost-effective, highly
sensitive, label-free drug screening tool for rapid detection and quantification of illicit substances in urine
samples, enabling timely medical intervention and public health monitoring. By expanding access to advanced
drug testing in resource-limited settings, this technology has the potential to reduce treatment delays, enhance
public safety, and alleviate the societal burden of substance misuse.

title: SBIR: Plant virus immunotherapy for solid tumors
text:
Solid tumors remain a major cause of cancer-related death, and current immunotherapy treatments often fail
due to immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment. This project aims to advance PX101, a plant virus-
based immunotherapy that is directly injected into tumors to disrupt immune suppression and stimulate a
systemic and durable anti-tumor immune response. If successful, this work will support the development of a
new class of safe, effective, and broadly applicable cancer immunotherapies.

title: Defining Functional Dynamics of Multidomain Redox Enzymes
text:
Proteins are often highly dynamic, and this flexibility is essential for function, but such motions often remain
largely unclear. To advance a fundamental understanding of functional protein dynamics, we will investigate
nitric oxide synthase (NOS), a family of paradigmatic multidomain proteins, using our integrative toolbox. The
methodology developed here promises to be useful for studying the differences among the NOS isoforms,
which in turn could be exploited to therapeutically target one NOS isoform over another.

title: Brain dynamics underlying long-term memory consolidation
text:
Memory consolidation is the gradual process of re-organizing memory representations from
their initial sites of encoding to more permanent storage. This process is disrupted in many
neurological and psychiatric conditions, however, due to technical limitations, little is understood
about this weeks-to-months long brain reorganization process. Here we develop new behavioral
paradigms and methods for chronic recording of relevant brain regions for at least one month to
gain insight into how some memories are forgotten while others are progressively stabilized.

title: Core Grant for Vision Research-LABORATORY COMPUTER APPLICATIONS MODULE (LCAM)
text: Laboratory Computer Applications Project Summary/Abstract The Laboratory Computer Applications Module (LCAM) provides support to individual and collaborative efforts by providing training in the advanced use of scientific software as well as research programming and consulting services for research projects. Furthermore, it supports all other core modules (Animal Resource, Flow Cytometry and Morphology) by managing the gathering, processing, and analyzing data on the various computerized systems at each module. The LCAM provides the expertise to facilitate real-time data transfers, convert image-based data to analytic forms, to update and purchase new and additional software, interconnect microcomputer systems between laboratories and equipment, to provide programming resources for such interfaces, and to facilitate analyses within laboratories. Finally, the LCAM supports the application and integration of machine learning algorithms for advanced imaging data analysis by providing a hardware and software infrastructure and the necessary training and consulting.

title: Preclinical imaging of immune responses to chronic stress
text:
In this project we propose to develop and apply novel and established position emission tomography methods
for preclinical assessment of stress-induced immune reprogramming in cardiovascular disease. Imaging will be
performed in a longitudinal fashion to study the immediate and long-term effects of psychosocial stress.

title: Understanding longitudinal microbiome change in relation to immunologic outcomes in pediatric SCT recipients.
text:
Allogeneic stem cell transplant (SCT) is a life-saving treatment for children with leukemia, immunodeficiencies,
and other disorders of the hematopoietic system, yet its success is limited by aberrant or delayed development
of the new immune system. The gastrointestinal tract microbiota, and microbiome disruption that occurs over the
course of SCT, may predict or even contribute to the pathogenesis of these immune-related outcomes, including
graft-versus-host disease and time to immune cell recovery. This study will further define the relationship
between microbiome disruption and immunologic outcomes of SCT, laying the foundation to develop new
biomarkers and therapeutic approaches to improve the success of this treatment.

title: Inside out: Revealing strategies for intracellular S. aureus persister eradication
text:
Antibiotic tolerance enables a subpopulation of genetically identical bacteria to withstand multiple antibiotics over
an extended duration, causing treatment failures and relapsing infections. The ability of Staphylococcus aureus–
one of the leading bacterial causes of death–to hide inside host mammalian cells and form tolerant persisters
largely reduces the therapeutic efficacy of antibiotics. I will use a combination of transcriptomic, pharmaceutical
and single-cell approaches to dissect the survival mechanisms of intracellular S. aureus persisters, aiming to
develop innovative strategies to control and eradicate this difficult-to-treat intracellular bacterial population.
